An Enhanced Low-Computational-Complexity
Predeﬁned-Time Convergent Zeroing Neural
Network for Constrained Time-Varying Quadratic
Programming With Kinematic Control of
Robotic Manipulator
Junpei Yang , Zhan Li , and Weibing Li , Member, IEEE
Abstract—Time-varying
quadratic
programming
(TVQP)
problems can be regarded as a challenging issue in a wide
range of engineering
applications,
frequently incorporating
equality, inequality, and bound constraints. By integrating a
nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) formulation, zero-
ing
neural
networks
(ZNNs)
can
be
generalized
to
solve
TVQP problems eﬀectively with such a full set of constraints.
However, three issues may limit its computational eﬃciency
and practical applications: 1) the inherent formulation of
NCP functions for handling equality/inequality and boundary
constraints substantially expands dimensions of coeﬃcient matri-
ces/vectors and solution-space variables; 2) the conventional
ZNN (CZNN) framework inevitably necessitates matrix inversion
operations for real-time solutions; and 3) insuﬃcient robustness
against noise interference compromises solution accuracy in
practical implementations. To overcome these issues and pro-
mote solution performance, this article develops an enhanced
lower dimension NCP low-computational-complexity (LCC) ZNN
(ELNCP-LCCZNN) model for solving TVQP problems with time-
varying equality, inequality, and variable boundary constraints.
An ELNCP function is designed to reduce the matrix/vector
coeﬃcients of the model, and the LCCZNN model is utilized
to construct a new dynamic model that eliminates the necessity
for matrix inversion during solution. Furthermore, a nonlinear
activation function is involved to guarantee predeﬁned-time
convergence and strengthen robustness against noise. The the-
oretical properties of the proposed ELNCP-LCCZNN model are
validated through numerical simulations and experiments on
robotic manipulator kinematic control. The results corroborate
the analysis and demonstrate improved computational eﬃciency,
enhanced noise robustness, and practical implementability com-
pared with existing approaches.

I. INTRODUCTION

RIVEN by the exponential growth of industrial automa-
tion and intelligent manufacturing technologies, robotic

as

increasing

[1], [2]. Kinematic control of robotic manipulators, which
reﬂects trajectory tracking in the workspace [3], directly
impacts operational eﬃciency and safety. In complex industrial
environments, robotic arm trajectory tracking must not only
meet dynamic performance requirements but also comply with
various physical and operational constraints, including obsta-
cle avoidance, joint limitations, and speed and acceleration
limits, which are typically formulated as multiple constraints.
The constrained kinematic control problem often aims to min-
imize quadratic cost functions related to energy consumption
[4], allocated task time [5], and kinematic positioning error
[6]. As a result, the trajectory tracking problem is generally
formulated as a time-varying quadratic programming (TVQP)
problem with equality, inequality, and boundary constraints
[7]. Therefore, the study of quadratic programming problems
with such constraints is essential for ensuring control per-
formance, reducing energy costs, and improving operational
safety.
Despite extensive research eﬀorts, the solution of TVQP
problems remains challenging due to three primary factors:
the increased dimensionality induced by inequality and bound-
ary constraints, the computational overhead introduced by
unavoidable matrix inversions, and inevitable noise that com-
promises accuracy and stability. To address these issues, this
article develops an enhanced lower dimensional nonlinear
complementarity problem (ELNCP)-based low-computational-
complexity (LCC) zeroing neural networks (ZNNs) for solving
TVQP problems, termed ELNCP-LCCZNN. By introduc-
ing an ELNCP function, the proposed approach eﬀectively

The eﬀectiveness of the proposed method is validated through
numerical simulations and physical experiments on a UR3(e)
robotic manipulator. In addition, Table I presents a systematic

The main contributions of this article are summarized as
follows.
1) An ELNCP-LCCZNN model is developed to solve the
TVQP problem with equality, inequality, and bound-
ary constraints. Relative to existing NCPs-LCCZNN
schemes, it reduces coeﬃcient-matrix dimensionality,
thereby improving computational eﬃciency for online
control.
2) Integrating the advanced AF into ELNCP-LCCZNN
guarantees predeﬁned-time convergence. This design
strengthens the predeﬁned-time convergence property
over existing ELNCP-based RNNs, enhancing suitability
for time-sensitive practical computations.
3) The
ELNCP-LCCZNN
model
demonstrates
robust
behavior under diverse noise perturbations and consis-
tently achieves lower residual errors than representative
ﬁnite-time convergent schemes.
4) Simulation and experiments on the UR3/UR3(e) manip-
ulators are conducted in cases without noise and with
noise, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed
model as compared to other methods for solving TVQP
problems.
II. RELATED WORKS
The constraint consists exclusively of either equality con-
straints (EC) or inequality constraints (IEC) formulations in
QP problems. Extensive studies on EC-QP problems have
led to rapid advancements and the development of promising
methods for obtaining feasible solutions. In contrast, IEC-QP
problems are more challenging and are commonly addressed
by transforming IECs into ECs, followed by the application
of EC-QP solvers.
A representative approach [8] introduces slack variables
to convert IECs into ECs. However, this method demands
high computational stability and a restricted choice of initial
points, as it may produce solutions that do not satisfy the
original IECs, thereby falling outside the feasible parame-
ter space. Furthermore, the introduction of slack variables
increases computational complexity by raising the problem’s
dimensionality. To mitigate these issues, Yu et al. [9] pro-
posed a penalty strategy combined with a varying-parameter
recurrent neural network (PS-VP-RNN), which employs both
inner and outer penalty functions to incorporate penalty
terms into problem formulations with EC and IEC, thereby
transforming the constrained problems into unconstrained
objective functions. In addition, inspired by the NCP [10],
a perturbed Fischer–Burmeister (pFB) function was inte-
grated into the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions [11],
thereby extending these conditions to include IECs. The
pFB function facilitates the conversion of KKT conditions
with IECs into ECs. Subsequently, Zhang et al. [12] devel-
oped an obstacle-variable parameter dynamic learning network
that integrates primitive NCP functions, penalty functions,
and slack variables. However, most existing transformation
strategies inevitably lead to increased problem dimensionality,
particularly in the presence of boundary constraints, which can
signiﬁcantly reduce computational eﬃciency.
Once transformed into EC-QP formulations, TVQP prob-
lems are traditionally solved using numerical optimization
methods such as the interior point method [13], gradient
projection method [14], and active-set method [15]. While
these methods perform well for static optimization, their
computational eﬃciency and real-time performance are often
insuﬃcient for time-varying scenarios. To overcome these
challenges, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) [16], [17] have
been widely investigated due to their parallel computation
capability and suitability for real-time hardware implemen-
tation. Early RNN-based approaches, including conventional
gradient neural networks (CGNNs) [18], have demonstrated
eﬀectiveness in solving dynamic optimization problems. How-
ever, CGNN models rely solely on gradient descent directions,
which can lead to persistent lagging residual errors in
time-varying environments. To overcome this issue, gradient
diﬀerential network (GDN) [19] and a fractional-order exten-
sion of the gradient neural framework [20] have been proposed
for solving TVQP problems.
More recently, a novel RNN based on a vector-valued func-
tion design, known as the conventional ZNN (CZNN) [21], has
attracted signiﬁcant attention for time-varying optimization.
One of CZNN’s key advantages is its ability to eliminate the
hysteresis residual errors observed in CGNN by incorporating
an additional time derivative of time-varying information,
thereby oﬀering a more accurate and robust solution. However,
current analyses indicate that the CZNN dynamics model
inevitably involves matrix inversion operations during its
solution process [22], [23], which degrades its computational
eﬃciency. In practical applications, such as kinematic con-
trol of robotic manipulators, there is a growing demand for
more accurate and robust trajectory tracking, and experi-
mental results [24] suggest that the performance of CZNN
deteriorates signiﬁcantly in the presence of disturbances. Con-
sequently, ongoing research is focused on enhancing these
aspects of CZNN performance. A critical factor inﬂuenc-
ing ZNN eﬀectiveness is the choice of AFs. For instance,
Zeng et al. [25] introduced symbolic double idempotent AFs to
facilitate ﬁnite-time convergence, while Jin et al. [6] proposed
predeﬁned ﬁxed-time convergent ZNN (PFT-ZNN), equipped
with a power piecewise AF that achieves predeﬁned-time
convergence. Furthermore, the design of the energy function
within the CZNN framework is crucial for determining overall
performance. Li et al. [26] and Li et al. [27] enhanced the
robustness of their models against disturbances by introduc-
ing integral energy functions and consequently proposed the
improved integral-enhanced ZNN (IIE-ZNN) and the triple
integral-enhanced ZNN (TIE-ZNN), respectively. Meanwhile,
Chen et al. [28] developed an LCCZNN model that replaces

II. RELATED WORKS
The constraint consists exclusively of either equality con-
straints (EC) or inequality constraints (IEC) formulations in
QP problems. Extensive studies on EC-QP problems have
led to rapid advancements and the development of promising
methods for obtaining feasible solutions. In contrast, IEC-QP
problems are more challenging and are commonly addressed
by transforming IECs into ECs, followed by the application
of EC-QP solvers.
A representative approach [8] introduces slack variables
to convert IECs into ECs. However, this method demands
high computational stability and a restricted choice of initial
points, as it may produce solutions that do not satisfy the
original IECs, thereby falling outside the feasible parame-
ter space. Furthermore, the introduction of slack variables
increases computational complexity by raising the problem’s
dimensionality. To mitigate these issues, Yu et al. [9] pro-
posed a penalty strategy combined with a varying-parameter
recurrent neural network (PS-VP-RNN), which employs both
inner and outer penalty functions to incorporate penalty
terms into problem formulations with EC and IEC, thereby
transforming the constrained problems into unconstrained
objective functions. In addition, inspired by the NCP [10],
a perturbed Fischer–Burmeister (pFB) function was inte-
grated into the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions [11],
thereby extending these conditions to include IECs. The
pFB function facilitates the conversion of KKT conditions
with IECs into ECs. Subsequently, Zhang et al. [12] devel-
oped an obstacle-variable parameter dynamic learning network
that integrates primitive NCP functions, penalty functions,
and slack variables. However, most existing transformation
strategies inevitably lead to increased problem dimensionality,
particularly in the presence of boundary constraints, which can
signiﬁcantly reduce computational eﬃciency.
Once transformed into EC-QP formulations, TVQP prob-
lems are traditionally solved using numerical optimization
methods such as the interior point method [13], gradient
projection method [14], and active-set method [15]. While
these methods perform well for static optimization, their
computational eﬃciency and real-time performance are often
insuﬃcient for time-varying scenarios. To overcome these
challenges, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) [16], [17] have
been widely investigated due to their parallel computation
capability and suitability for real-time hardware implemen-
tation. Early RNN-based approaches, including conventional
gradient neural networks (CGNNs) [18], have demonstrated
eﬀectiveness in solving dynamic optimization problems. How-
ever, CGNN models rely solely on gradient descent directions,
which can lead to persistent lagging residual errors in
time-varying environments. To overcome this issue, gradient
diﬀerential network (GDN) [19] and a fractional-order exten-
sion of the gradient neural framework [20] have been proposed
for solving TVQP problems.
More recently, a novel RNN based on a vector-valued func-
tion design, known as the conventional ZNN (CZNN) [21], has
attracted signiﬁcant attention for time-varying optimization.
One of CZNN’s key advantages is its ability to eliminate the
hysteresis residual errors observed in CGNN by incorporating
an additional time derivative of time-varying information,
thereby oﬀering a more accurate and robust solution. However,
current analyses indicate that the CZNN dynamics model
inevitably involves matrix inversion operations during its
solution process [22], [23], which degrades its computational
eﬃciency. In practical applications, such as kinematic con-
trol of robotic manipulators, there is a growing demand for
more accurate and robust trajectory tracking, and experi-
mental results [24] suggest that the performance of CZNN
deteriorates signiﬁcantly in the presence of disturbances. Con-
sequently, ongoing research is focused on enhancing these
aspects of CZNN performance. A critical factor inﬂuenc-

Zeng et al. [25] introduced symbolic double idempotent AFs to
facilitate ﬁnite-time convergence, while Jin et al. [6] proposed
predeﬁned ﬁxed-time convergent ZNN (PFT-ZNN), equipped
with a power piecewise AF that achieves predeﬁned-time
convergence. Furthermore, the design of the energy function
within the CZNN framework is crucial for determining overall
performance. Li et al. [26] and Li et al. [27] enhanced the
robustness of their models against disturbances by introduc-

VI. CONCLUSION
This article proposes an ELNCP-LCCZNN model equipped
with the STPEAF to address bounded constrained TVQP
problems. By integrating a novel reduced-dimension NCP
function into the LCCZNN framework, the proposed approach
further decreases computational complexity while preserving
convergence and robustness properties. Numerical simulations
demonstrate that the proposed method signiﬁcantly reduces
the physical solution time compared with existing boundary
constraint handling approaches, resulting in a faster sys-
tem response. Furthermore, comprehensive comparisons with
state-of-the-art RNN methods demonstrate that the proposed
framework achieves superior overall performance in terms of
convergence speed, solution accuracy, and robustness against
noise. Simulation and experimental results on the UR3 and
UR3e robot platforms validate the capability of the proposed
approach to provide rapid response and strong noise rejection,
as well as its feasibility and stability in practical applications.
Future work will extend this framework to higher dimensional
systems, more complex constraint conditions, and multiobjec-
tive optimization scenarios.
